name: Timing Diagram
description: Timing Diagram describes the change of state or value of a lifeline along a linear time axis. This diagram is especially useful for real-time, embedded, or strict timing constraint systems.
purpose: Analyze latency, duration constraints, deadlines, or timeouts in real-time systems.
bestFor: Design real-time hardware or embedded systems
Describe latency, duration constraints, deadlines, or timeouts
Analyze object state/value changes per ms/s
Design automatic lock/unlock mechanisms over time
notSuitableFor: Describe general transition logic → use State Machine Diagram
Describe messages between services → use Sequence Diagram
Describe business workflow → use Activity Diagram
useCases: Identify lifelines to monitor over time
Draw state/value levels along the vertical axis
Mark state changes at specific time points
requirements: States/Values — states along the vertical axis
Time events — time points causing state changes (optional)

elements.name: State/Value
elements.description: States or values along the vertical axis: Open, Closed, Locked

elements.name: Time Event
elements.description: Time point or event causing state change

confusableWith.difference: Timing emphasizes states over specific time; State Machine emphasizes transition/event logic.
Sequence emphasizes message order; Timing emphasizes duration and state/value over timeline.
